run.question:
The checkout-service in production-eu-west-2 is throwing 500s. Please look at
app-264-prod-logs and find the root cause.

report.summary: No evidence exists in this Run for the environment the question names, production-eu-west-2. The only index that exists is app-264-prod-logs, and every document in it carries cluster="staging-eu-west-2" and environment="staging" (region eu-west-2): 3 documents in total inside the authorized window 2026-10-24T17:41:26Z–2026-11-23T17:41:26Z (source samples 2026-11-23T15:41:19Z to 2026-11-23T17:11:19Z). Nothing in those documents is production telemetry, so none of it can be named as the root cause of a production checkout-service incident; it is reported below strictly as staging-eu-west-2 data. The three staging documents are: checkout-service ERROR "Smoke test failed: deploy-v2.3.4 rollback in progress" (2026-11-23T15:41:19Z), checkout-service ERROR "POST /api/checkout returned 500: integration-test fixture stripe-test-key expired" (2026-11-23T16:41:19Z), and payment-service WARN "Using mock provider for staging (stripe-mock)" (2026-11-23T17:11:19Z). Prometheus and Jaeger were both unreachable (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE) in this Run, so no error-rate, latency or trace evidence could be obtained for any cluster, and Kubernetes access only covers the staging-eu-west-2 cluster (otel-demo namespace), where checkout is ready with 0 restarts. Conclusion: inconclusive for production-eu-west-2; no root cause named.

claims.text: Only one index exists in the log store: app-264-prod-logs (green, 3 documents, 7.7kb). Its mapped fields are cluster, environment, level, message, region, service and timestamp (a date field), so the index name's "prod" does not by itself establish which cluster or environment the documents belong to.

Inside the authorized window app-264-prod-logs contains exactly 3 documents (total relation eq, 3 returned, no shard failures), and every one of them carries cluster="staging-eu-west-2", environment="staging" and region="eu-west-2". Term aggregations over the whole index return a single cluster bucket (staging-eu-west-2, 3 docs) and a single environment bucket (staging, 3 docs); no document with cluster="production-eu-west-2" is present in the returned set.

The staging-eu-west-2 documents are two ERROR lines from service checkout-service and one WARN line from service payment-service, at 2026-11-23T15:41:19Z ("Smoke test failed: deploy-v2.3.4 rollback in progress"), 2026-11-23T16:41:19Z ("POST /api/checkout returned 500: integration-test fixture stripe-test-key expired") and 2026-11-23T17:11:19Z ("Using mock provider for staging (stripe-mock)"). Levels in the index are ERROR 2 and WARN 1; services are checkout-service 2 and payment-service 1.

In the only cluster I can read, staging-eu-west-2, the checkout workload is not degraded at query time: Deployment checkout in namespace otel-demo has 1 ready replica on image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout, and its pod checkout-6578865d87-v6flf is Running, its container checkout ready=true with restartCount 0 and no previous terminated instance. This is a staging-eu-west-2 observation and says nothing about production-eu-west-2.

For staging-eu-west-2 only: the logged checkout-service 500 is attributed by its own message to an expired integration-test credential ("integration-test fixture stripe-test-key expired"), and payment-service logs the use of the staging stripe mock. This is a staging hypothesis about staging traffic and is not evidence of, and is not offered as, the production-eu-west-2 root cause.

Also staging-only and unverified as a cause of anything: the ERROR line reports "deploy-v2.3.4 rollback in progress" at 2026-11-23T15:41:19Z, i.e. a staging deploy change inside the window. No Kubernetes evidence ties it to a production rollout, and no change-history integration is available to confirm what changed.

gaps: No production-eu-west-2 data exists in any available source: the only log index, app-264-prod-logs, contains 3 documents and all are labelled cluster=staging-eu-west-2 / environment=staging. Whether production-eu-west-2 checkout-service is throwing 500s, and why, could not be observed.

Prometheus was unreachable in this Run: get_all_labels, get_label_values and execute_prometheus_instant_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate, request-rate or latency series (e.g. traces_span_metrics_calls_total, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count, kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready) could be read for any cluster, and no baseline exists for a latency comparison.

Jaeger was unreachable: traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no trace or span-level evidence (status codes, error spans, parent-child call edges) is available for checkout-service in any cluster.

Kubernetes access covers only the staging-eu-west-2 cluster, so production-eu-west-2 Deployment/Pod/Service/ConfigMap objects for checkout-service could not be inspected. The otel-demo namespace I read is staging, and it contains no Service or ConfigMap objects for a production environment.
No Kubernetes events were returned for the authorized window (events query returned no_data, 0 items processed), so cluster-level evidence about any restart, eviction or scheduling event is missing.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so what was deployed or changed in production-eu-west-2 during the incident window is unknown.

The checkout pod log query on staging (filter error|fail|500|exception|panic|stripe, 300 lines read, 297 dropped by the filter, 3 dropped as outside the window) returned no matching lines and has status no_data; this cannot be cited as proof that staging checkout logged no errors, and it says nothing about production.
next_steps: Confirm where production-eu-west-2 application logs are shipped: the index named app-264-prod-logs is receiving staging-eu-west-2 documents only, so the production checkout-service log stream appears to be missing or misrouted.
Once production log/metric/trace ingestion is verified, re-check checkout-service 500s in production-eu-west-2 and compare with its payment dependency's credentials and provider configuration.
Inspect the staging-eu-west-2 deploy-v2.3.4 rollback and the expired stripe-test-key fixture as a separate staging issue, not as the production cause.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
